arxiv-1808-03951.title: Measurement of the azimuthal anisotropy of charged particles produced in s NN \sqrt{s_{{}_{\text{NN}}}} = 5.02 TeV Pb+Pb collisions with the ATLAS detector
arxiv-1808-03951.creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
arxiv-1808-03951.description: Abstract Measurements of the azimuthal anisotropy in lead–lead collisions at s NN \sqrt{s_{{}_{\text{NN}}}} = 5.02 TeV are presented using a data sample corresponding to 0.49 nb − 1 \mathrm{nb}^{-1} integrated luminosity collected by the ATLAS experiment at the LHC in 2015.

arxiv-2107-05129.title: Bremsstrahlung photons from stopping in heavy-ion collisions
arxiv-2107-05129.creator: Sohyun Park, Urs Achim Wiedemann
arxiv-2107-05129.description: Abstract We examine the spectrum of bremsstrahlung photons that results from the stopping of the initial net charge distributions in ultrarelativistic nucleus-nucleus collisions at the CERN Large Hadron Collier (LHC). This effect has escaped detection so far since it becomes sizable only at very low transverse momentum and at sufficiently forward rapidity.

arxiv-2111-01209.title: Local simultaneous state discrimination
arxiv-2111-01209.creator: Christian Majenz, Maris Ozols, Christian Schaffner, Mehrdad Tahmasbi
arxiv-2111-01209.description: Abstract Quantum state discrimination is one of the most fundamental problems studied in quantum information theory. Applications range from channel coding to metrology and cryptography. In this work, we introduce a new variant of this task: Local Simultaneous State Discrimination (LSSD).

arxiv-2112-15197.title: Collision-induced radiative quenching and other disintegration modes of the 2 ​ s 2s state of muonic hydrogen and deuterium atoms
arxiv-2112-15197.creator: V.P. Popov, V.N. Pomerantsev
arxiv-2112-15197.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by V.P. Popov, V.N. Pomerantsev. The formation and various disintegration modes of 2 ​ s 2s states for muonic hydrogen and deuterium atoms at kinetic energies both above and below the 2 ​ s − 2 ​ p 2s-2p threshold are studied.

arxiv-2203-12108.title: Efficient, ever-ready quantum memory at room temperature for single photons
arxiv-2203-12108.creator: Anthony C. Leung, 1,2† W. Y. Sarah Lau, 1,2,3,4† Aaron D. Tranter, 1,2 Karun V. Paul, 1,2 Markus Rambach, 3,4 Ben C. Buchler, 1,2 Ping Koy Lam, 1,2 Andrew G. White, 3,4 Till J. Weinhold 3,4∗ 1 ARC Centre of Excellence for Quantum Computation and Communication Technology 2 Department of Quantum Scien
arxiv-2203-12108.description: Abstract Efficient quantum memories will be an essential building block of large scale networked quantum systems and provide a link between flying photonic qubits and atomic or quasi-atomic local quantum processors. To provide a path to scalability avoidance of bulky, difficult to maintain systems such as high vacuum and low temperature cryogenics is imperative.

arxiv-2210-14205.title: Unit Averaging for Heterogeneous Panels
arxiv-2210-14205.creator: Christian Brownlees, Vladislav Morozov
arxiv-2210-14205.description: Abstract In this work we introduce a unit averaging procedure to efficiently recover unit-specific parameters in a heterogeneous panel model. The procedure consists in estimating the parameter of a given unit using a weighted average of all the unit-specific parameter estimators in the panel. The weights of the average are determined by minimizing an MSE criterion we derive.

arxiv-2408-04726.title: Random search with resetting in heterogeneous environments
arxiv-2408-04726.creator: Luiz Menon Jr. 1 , and Celia Anteneodo 1,2
arxiv-2408-04726.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Luiz Menon Jr. 1 , and Celia Anteneodo 1,2. We investigate random searches under stochastic position resetting at rate r r , in a bounded 1D environment with space-dependent diffusivity D ⁡ ( x ) D(x) . For arbitrary shapes of D ⁡ ( x ) D(x) and prescriptions of the associated multiplicative stochastic process, we obtain analytical expressions for the average time T T for reaching the target (mean first-passage time), given the initial and reset positions, in good agreement with stochastic simulations.

arxiv-2410-13376.title: Data-Augmented Predictive Deep Neural Network: Enhancing the extrapolation capabilities of non-intrusive surrogate models
arxiv-2410-13376.creator: Shuwen Sun, Lihong Feng, Peter Benner
arxiv-2410-13376.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Shuwen Sun, Lihong Feng, Peter Benner. Numerically solving a large parametric nonlinear dynamical system is challenging due to its high complexity and the high computational costs. In recent years, machine-learning-aided surrogates are being actively researched. However, many methods fail in accurately generalizing in the entire time interval [ 0 , T ] [0,T] , when the training data is available only in a training time interval [ 0 , T 0 ] [0,T_{0}] , with T 0 < T T_{0}<T .

The problem in its general form can be stated as follows. MinRank Problem .

arxiv-2511-17772.title: Weighted Birkhoff Averages Accelerate Data-Driven Methods
arxiv-2511-17772.creator: Maria Bou-Sakr-El-Tayar, Jason J. Bramburger, Matthew J. Colbrook
arxiv-2511-17772.description: Abstract Many data-driven algorithms in dynamical systems rely on ergodic averages that converge painfully slowly. One simple idea changes this: taper the ends. Weighted Birkhoff averages can converge much faster (sometimes superpolynomially, even exponentially) and can be incorporated seamlessly into existing methods.

arxiv-2512-11643.title: Stateless Snowflake: A Cloud-Agnostic Distributed ID Generator Using Network-Derived Identity
arxiv-2512-11643.creator: Manideep Reddy Chinthareddy
arxiv-2512-11643.description: Abstract Snowflake-style distributed ID generators are the industry standard for producing k k -ordered, unique identifiers at scale. However, the traditional requirement for manually assigned or centrally coordinated worker IDs introduces significant friction in modern container-orchestrated environments (e.g., Kubernetes), where workloads are ephemeral and autoscaled.

britannica-1911-hungerford-walter-hunger.title: Hungerford, Walter Hungerford, Baron (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-hungerford-walter-hunger.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-hungerford-walter-hunger.description: Article 'Hungerford, Walter Hungerford, Baron' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 13), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. English soldier, belonged to a Wiltshire family. His father, Sir Thomas Hungerford (d. 1398), was speaker of the House of Commons in 1377, a position which he owed to his friend John of Gaunt, and is the first person formally mentioned in the rolls of parliament as holding the office.

pmc-10727650.title: Exploring the pharmacological and molecular mechanisms of Salvia chinensis Benth in colorectal cancer: A network pharmacology and molecular docking study
pmc-10727650.creator: Qian Zheng, Xin Wang, Tian Gao, Bingzhou Zhang, Ning Zhao, Runsen Du, Zengren Zhao
pmc-10727650.description: While Salvia chinensis Benth (commonly known as “Shijianchuan” in Chinese, and abbreviated as SJC) is commonly used in adjuvant therapy for colorectal cancer (CRC) in traditional Chinese medicine, its mechanism of action remains unclear. In this study, Initially, we examined the impact of SJC on CRC cells in an in vitro setting.

pmc-10746989.title: Combining Cisplatin with Different Radiation Qualities—Interpretation of Cytotoxic Effects In Vitro by Isobolographic Analysis
pmc-10746989.creator: Roswitha Runge, Falco Reissig, Nora Herzog, Liane Oehme, Claudia Brogsitter, Joerg Kotzerke, Hirofumi Hanaoka
pmc-10746989.description: Background: The combination of platinum-containing cytostatic drugs with different radiation qualities has been studied for years. Despite their massive side effects, these drugs still belong to the therapeutic portfolio in cancer treatment. To overcome the disadvantages of cisplatin, our study investigated the cytotoxic effects of combining radionuclides with cisplatin.

pmc-11528959.title: Comparing adaptations from blood flow restriction exercise training using regulated or unregulated pressure systems: A systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-11528959.creator: Matthew J Clarkson, Breanna McMahon, Stuart A Warmington
pmc-11528959.description: ObjectiveNo study has examined outcomes derived from blood flow restriction exercise training interventions using regulated compared with unregulated blood flow restriction pressure systems. Therefore, we used a systematic review and meta-analyses to compare the chronic adaptations to blood flow restriction exercise training achieved with regulated and unregulated blood flow restriction pressure systems.

pmc-13079642.title: How generative AI enhances self-regulated learning in EFL learners: a chain mediation model of “intention to use” and “learning engagement”
pmc-13079642.creator: Jin Xu
pmc-13079642.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Generative Artificial Intelligence is transforming English as a Foreign Language writing instruction. While much research has focused on technology acceptance, limited attention has been paid to how AI influences learners’ psychological and behavioral processes, thereby affecting self-regulated learning. This study constructs and tests a theoretical model that examines the chain mediation of “intention to use → learning engagement” to explore how generative AI impacts self-regulated learning in EFL learners.

pmc-13507671.title: Associations between digital health literacy and health inequalities among middle-aged and older adults: an urban–rural disparity perspective
pmc-13507671.creator: Jian Wu, Pingping An, Ning Chen
pmc-13507671.description: BackgroundIn the digital age, digital health literacy has emerged as a critical factor influencing the physical and mental well-being of middle-aged and older adults. However, the relationship between digital health literacy and health inequalities remains underexplored. This study aims to investigate this association among middle-aged and older adults in urban and rural settings.
